title: The Emperor Who Was a Stoic

panels.visual: Emperor Marcus Aurelius (bearded, simple cloak over armour) writing in a tent in a military camp by lamplight at night, a scroll and a stylus, soldiers' fires outside
panels.caption: Marcus Aurelius, emperor of Rome, wrote notes to himself in Greek, night after night: the Meditations.

panels.visual: Marcus's hand writing on a scroll with the lamp glow, a swirl of the words beside it, a calm face
panels.caption: You cannot control what others do, only what you do.

panels.visual: Marcus sitting on the edge of a narrow camp bed on a cold morning wrapped in a blanket, grumpy and sleepy, his breath steaming, getting up with effort
panels.caption: On mornings he dreaded, he told himself to get up.

speech.speaker: Marcus
speech.text: Get up. I was made to work with others, like hands and feet.

panels.visual: Athens in AD 176: Marcus on the Acropolis steps pointing at four professors at four lecterns shown as four vignettes in a row: a Platonist with a circle diagram, an Aristotelian with a cat and notebook, a Stoic under a porch and an Epicurean in a garden
panels.caption: In AD 176 he visited Athens and paid for four professors of philosophy.
